nct.text: Not applicable — efficacy demonstrated in animal models under the Animal Rule; no human efficacy trial / NCT

citations.quote: Because it is not feasible or ethical to conduct controlled clinical trials in humans with inhalational anthrax, the efficacy of ANTHIM for the treatment of inhalational anthrax is based on efficacy studies in NZW rabbits and cynomolgus macaques.

The effectiveness of ANTHIM is based solely on efficacy studies in animal models of inhalational anthrax. It is not ethical or feasible to conduct controlled clinical trials with intentional exposure of humans to anthrax [see *Clinical Studies* (14)].

indication.text: Indicated in adult and pediatric patients for treatment of inhalational anthrax due to B. anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs, and for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or not appropriate.

citations.quote: ANTHIM is indicated in adult and pediatric patients for the treatment of inhalational anthrax due to *Bacillus anthracis* in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs.
ANTHIM is indicated for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax due to *B. anthracis* when alternative therapies are not available or not appropriate [see *Indications and Usage* (1.2)].

target_moa.text: Monoclonal antibody that binds free protective antigen (PA) of B. anthracis toxin (Kd 0.33 nM), inhibiting PA binding to its cellular receptors and preventing intracellular entry of anthrax lethal factor and edema factor; it has no direct antibacterial activity.

citations.quote: Obiltoxaximab is a monoclonal antibody that binds free PA with an affinity equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.33 nM. Obiltoxaximab inhibits the binding of PA to its cellular receptors, preventing the intracellular entry of the anthrax lethal factor and edema factor, the enzymatic toxin components responsible for the pathogenic effects of anthrax toxin.
ANTHIM binds to the protective antigen (PA) component of *B. anthracis* toxin; it does not have direct antibacterial activity.

modality.text: mAb (chimeric IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody, ~148 kDa)

citations.quote: Obiltoxaximab is a chimeric IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds the PA component of *B. anthracis* toxin. It has an approximate molecular weight of 148 kDa.

key_safety.text: Safety studied only in 320 healthy volunteers. Hypersensitivity reactions were the most common adverse reactions, occurring in 34/320 (10.6%), with 3 (0.9%) cases of anaphylaxis. Most frequent adverse reactions (single-dose ANTHIM vs placebo) included headache (8% vs 6%), pruritus (4% vs 1%), and upper respiratory tract infections (5% vs 3%).

detail.text: Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis have been reported during IV infusion of ANTHIM; administer in monitored settings by personnel trained and equipped to manage anaphylaxis, monitor closely, and stop infusion immediately if hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis occurs.

citations.quote: Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis have been reported during the intravenous infusion of ANTHIM. Due to the risk of hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis, ANTHIM should be administered in monitored settings by personnel trained and equipped to manage anaphylaxis. Monitor individuals who receive ANTHIM closely for signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity reactions throughout the infusion and for a period of time after administration. Stop ANTHIM infusion immediately and treat appropriately if hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis occurs [see *Indications and Usage* (1.2), *Dosage and Administration* (2.4) and *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)].

summary.text: Anthim (obiltoxaximab) was approved under 21 CFR 601 Subpart H (Animal Rule), because human efficacy studies are not ethical or feasible; efficacy was established in animal models of inhalational anthrax while safety was evaluated in healthy human volunteers. The product held Fast Track designation (2006) and Orphan Drug Designation (2006), was reviewed as a standard application, and was not referred to an Advisory Committee.
